findings.title: Migration raises NoMethodError when the old settings rows are absent
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query always returns at least one row. On any site where `embed_category` was never set (the default was `''`, so no `site_settings` row exists at all) or where its value no longer matches a category name, the result set is empty and `[0]` is `nil`, so `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError and the whole migration aborts. The same problem exists on line 15: `uncategorized_category_id` defaults to `-1` and is normally not persisted in `site_settings`, so that fallback query also returns zero rows and crashes. Both lookups need to handle an empty result (and the resulting `category_id` must be a real category, since the column is `null: false` and `-1` points at nothing).

findings.title: Migration copies host values verbatim, so hosts that included a scheme stop matching
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` site setting explicitly allowed entries such as `http://discourse.org` (the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped the scheme at comparison time, and the removed specs covered exactly that). This migration inserts each line directly with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing the model's `before_validation` that strips `https?://` and paths. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then compares `lower(host)` against `URI(...).host` (a bare hostname), so a migrated row `http://discourse.org` can never match and embedding/topic retrieval silently breaks for those sites. Because line 31 deletes the `embeddable_hosts` setting, the original data is also gone and cannot be re-migrated. Normalize the value (strip scheme/path, downcase) before inserting.

findings.title: Host value interpolated into SQL without quoting
findings.body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates an admin-supplied site-setting value straight into SQL. A value containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacter) produces a syntax error and aborts the migration mid-way — after the table was created and before the old settings are deleted — leaving the site in an inconsistent state. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or a parameterized `execute`/model insert.

findings.title: has_many embed: :ids does not side-load the hosts the client needs
findings.body: With ActiveModel::Serializers 0.8 (the version this codebase uses), `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` emits only `embeddable_host_ids`; the host objects are side-loaded into the root payload only when `include: true`/`embed_in_root: true` is also given. The Ember store resolves plural foreign keys in `_hydrateEmbedded` by looking up `root[pluralize(subType)]` (i.e. a root-level `embeddable_hosts` array) — see the matching test fixture that returns `{__rest_serializer: "1", fruits, farmers, colors}`. Without the side-loaded array every id resolves to `undefined`, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined` and the admin table renders empty/broken rows. Add `include: true` (or `embed: :objects`) and a controller spec asserting the JSON contains the hosts.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` is executed in a `before_validation` callback without a nil check. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which is `nil` when the client omits/blanks the field, and `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` is also legitimate. In that case `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500 instead of the intended `validates_format_of` validation error. Guard the callback (e.g. `return if host.blank?`) and add `validates_presence_of :host`.

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the parameter side
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value extracted from the request: `URI("http://Example.com").host` returns `Example.com` with its original case. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://Example.com/page` (or a stored host entered with capitals) will not match any row, and `host_allowed?` returns false — `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` then raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` and `TopicRetriever` refuses to fetch, silently breaking embedding. Downcase the argument: `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`.

findings.title: update/destroy dereference nil when the id does not exist
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` for an unknown or already-deleted id. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which hits `nil.host=` and `destroy` (line 16) calls `nil.destroy`, both raising NoMethodError and producing a 500 instead of a 404. This is easy to trigger from the admin UI by deleting the same host twice (or from two browser tabs). Use `find_by`/`find` with an explicit `raise Discourse::NotFound` or `render json: ... , status: 404`.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that reports success
findings.body: `update` only re-renders the freshly fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct; it never reads params or persists anything, yet it returns 200 with the serialized object. The admin controller action `saveChanges` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6) calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` against this endpoint, so any future caller believes a save succeeded when nothing was written. Either implement the update or remove the route, the action and the controller method so no caller depends on a fake success.

findings.title: Plural embedded ids are dropped even when they cannot be resolved
findings.body: The new `m[2]` branch unconditionally does `obj[pluralize(subType)] = obj[k].map(id => this._lookupSubType(...))` and then `delete obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which keeps the `_id` key when hydration fails), this destroys the original ids: if the sub-collection is not side-loaded in the payload, the model ends up with an array of `undefined` values and the `*_ids` property is gone, so callers can neither use the objects nor fall back to the ids. It also assumes the value is an array — any REST-serialized attribute whose name happens to end in `_ids` but holds a string/number will throw `obj[k].map is not a function` and break hydration of the whole record. Only replace the key when every lookup succeeded (and guard with `Array.isArray`).

findings.title: New admin endpoints have no behavioural tests
findings.body: The only assertion in this spec (and in spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. Nothing exercises `create`, `update`, `destroy`, the uncategorized-category fallback, the staff/admin constraint, or the JSON shape of `GET /admin/customize/embedding`. As a result none of the new code paths are covered — including the serialization of the `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (a non-ActiveModel object handed to `EmbeddingSerializer`) and the nil-record handling in update/destroy. Add request specs that create/update/delete a host and assert the rendered payload.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The two file bodies were clearly exchanged; this works only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, and it makes the category fabricators impossible to find by filename. Swap the contents back.

findings.title: /fruits/:id handler ignores the requested id, making the new assertions vacuous
findings.body: The handler always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`) regardless of `request.params.id`. The updated store test now calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `colors` are ids 1 and 2, but fruit 2 (banana) has `color_ids: [3]` — the test passes only because the wrong record is served. The test therefore does not verify that the right record's `*_ids` are hydrated. Make the handler look the fruit up by id (`fruits.findBy('id', parseInt(request.params.id))`) so the assertions mean what they claim.

findings.title: Only the first underscore is dasherized when matching ADMIN_MODELS
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces a single occurrence, so a type with two or more underscores (e.g. `site_customization_thing`) becomes `site-customization_thing` and will not match its dasherized entry in `ADMIN_MODELS`, silently routing the request to `/` instead of `/admin/` and returning 404/403. Use a global replacement (`type.replace(/_/g, '-')`) or `Ember.String.dasherize(type)`.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same `host` (the migration creates no unique index and the model has no `validates_uniqueness_of :host`). `record_for_host` takes `.first` of the match, so when duplicates exist the category used for newly imported embedded topics is whichever row the database happens to return — a non-deterministic result that is confusing to debug. The column is also queried on every embed request with `lower(host) = ?` and has no index. Add a (case-insensitive) unique index plus a model validation.

findings.title: create_table with force: true in a migration can drop an existing table
findings.body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If the table already exists (e.g. this migration is re-run after a partial failure, or a multisite tenant already has the table), all existing embeddable host rows are destroyed without warning. Additionally, because `change` contains `execute` statements, the migration is not reversible and `rake db:rollback` will fail; use explicit `up`/`down` methods and drop `force: true`.

findings.title: Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts at all (the check was removed from app/models/topic.rb), so this example passes merely because `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for a built topic. The name claims coverage that does not exist and will mislead anyone debugging embedding. Either delete it or rename it to describe what it actually asserts.
